title: ControlNet
interviewAnswer: ControlNet adds a trainable conditioning branch to a pretrained diffusion model so structural signals such as edges, depth or poses can guide generation while preserving much of the pretrained backbone.
why: ControlNet is a practical way to add structural conditioning to pretrained diffusion models while preserving much of the base model capability.
intuition: Create a trainable branch that processes a control signal such as edges, depth or pose, then inject its features into a mostly frozen diffusion backbone.
deepDive: ControlNet copies/augments parts of the pretrained network and uses zero-initialized connections so the added branch starts with minimal disturbance to the base model. The control encoder learns spatial guidance aligned with the denoising network. It is useful when text/semantic embeddings are insufficient to preserve geometry.
workedExample: Canny edges from a microstructure can guide boundary layout while SDXL provides realistic texture/style variation.
commonMistakes: Assuming the whole base diffusion model must be retrained.
Using noisy/incorrect control maps without evaluating sensitivity.
followUps: What control signals can be used?
How do you balance control strength and diversity?
production: Control preprocessing becomes part of the serving contract; version edge/depth extraction settings with the model and monitor failures when controls are sparse/noisy.
